title: Break a Palindrome
statement:
The string `palindrome` reads the same forwards and backwards and uses only lowercase English letters. Change exactly one of its characters to some lowercase letter (it must differ from the original letter) so that the new string is **not** a palindrome. Among all strings you can get this way, return the lexicographically smallest one. If no single change can break the palindrome, return the empty string `""`.

For two strings of equal length, the lexicographically smaller one is the one with the smaller letter at the first index where they differ.
constraints: palindrome contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every position and every letter, then checking each result, works but wastes effort. To get the smallest string, we want to make the earliest possible character smaller, and the smallest letter is `'a'`. So find the first character that is not `'a'` and turn it into `'a'`.

Only the first half matters. Changing a character in the first half breaks the match with its mirror, so the result is no longer a palindrome. The middle character of an odd-length string has no partner: changing it leaves a palindrome, so it must be skipped.

If the first half is all `'a'`, any decrease is impossible. The least harmful change is then the latest one: turn the last character into `'b'`. A string of length 1 is a palindrome whatever its letter, so there is no answer.

## Approach

1. If `n` is 1, return `""`.
2. Copy the string into the array `chars`.
3. Scan `i` over the first half, `0` to `n / 2 - 1`. At the first `chars[i]` that is not `'a'`, set it to `'a'` and return the joined string.
4. Otherwise the first half is all `'a'`: set the last character to `'b'` and return.

## Example 1, step by step

`palindrome = "abccba"`, `n = 6`, so `i` checks indices 0 to 2. `chars[0]` is `'a'`, so it is skipped. `chars[1]` is `'b'`, so it becomes `'a'`, giving `"aaccba"`, which is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one scan of half the string plus building the result.
- Space: O(n) for the character array (strings are immutable).

## Pitfalls

- Do not scan past the first half: in `"aba"` changing the middle `'b'` to `'a'` gives `"aaa"`, still a palindrome. The right answer is `"abb"`.
- For an all-`'a'` string, change the *last* character to `'b'`; changing the first gives a larger string.
- Length 1 has no answer, even for a letter other than `'a'`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `palindrome` |
| `chars` | editable copy of the string |
| `i` | index in the first half being checked |

narration.2: Remember the length; it decides which half to scan.

narration.4: ...so no change can break it: return the empty string.
narration.7: Strings cannot be edited in place, so work on an array of characters.
narration.8: Scan only the first half; the middle of an odd length has no mirror to break.
narration.9: The first letter that is not 'a' can be made smaller.
narration.10: Turning it into 'a' makes the earliest possible position as small as possible.
narration.11: Its mirror still holds the old letter, so this is no longer a palindrome; return it.
narration.15: The first half is all 'a': the cheapest damage is raising the last letter to 'b'.
narration.16: Return the string with its last letter changed.
